::: {.lede}
I'm Wes Knipe, an economist by training and a builder by habit. AI agents have started paying for things on their own, and nobody seemed to be checking the receipts, so I started checking them.
:::

::: {.bio}
I studied quantitative economics at Cal Poly, with a minor in statistics, and spent the years since in early-stage software: customer interviews, go-to-market, a churn model, a product relaunch, and one very memorable first sale. Before that I was a financial advisor, long enough to pass three licensing exams in two months, and short enough to leave for startups and see how products and companies actually get built. These days I consult on analytics projects and build research tools, including Opportunity Atlas, a pipeline whose whole job is catching AI when it is confidently wrong.

I do my best work on long, ambiguous problems, and agent payments is one. Most of what gets said about it is volume, and most of the volume turns out to be agents paying themselves. So this site counts what's left after the loops, the self-dealing and the tests come out (about half, as of this week), and every number says what it's out of. A percentage without a denominator is just a mood.

I live in Santa Cruz. I also hold an FAA drone license, which has come up less often than you'd think.
:::

## What this site is

Independent, reproducible data on what AI agents actually buy and pay for:

- the demand-cleaned x402 index and its [market dashboard](/x402/);
- [seller](/x402/sellers/), [buyer](/x402/buyers/) and [price](/x402/prices/) statistics;
- a daily [endpoint monitor](/x402/status/) and a weekly [census of AI-crawler access](/access/);
- tools such as [Best execution](/x402/buy/), [Price comps](/x402/prices/comps) and the [AI-policy checker](/check/).

[x402scan](https://www.x402scan.com) is the raw explorer. This site is the part after cleaning: what survives, what buyers actually pay, and who comes back for more.

It's built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from a [public repository](https://github.com/doescodinggiteasier/wknipe-site), using only public data: Base chain transactions via Blockscout and the Coinbase CDP Bazaar listing. The [method note](https://github.com/doescodinggiteasier/wknipe-site/blob/main/docs/X402_INDEX_METHOD.md) lists every filter and every bias I know about. If you find one I don't, I'd like to hear it.

**My own payments are excluded.** I run a paid API for the index at `api.wknipe.com`. Payments to it, and from my test wallet, are tagged and never counted as demand. Grading my own homework seemed like a bad look.

**My crawlers.** The endpoint monitor (`wknipe-x402-status/1.0`) sends at most one unpaid request per listed endpoint per day, and no more than 60 per host. The access census (`wknipe-policy-check/1.0`) reads four small files per domain once a week. Both say who they are. To be left out, email wes@wknipe.com.

**Privacy.** Visits are counted with Cloudflare Web Analytics: no cookies, no personal data, no cross-site tracking. The [AI-policy checker](check/index.qmd) keeps each domain's result for 24 hours and logs nothing about who asked.
